investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GET (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the venue's official ticket-shop homepage (which is a real, server-rendered event listing, not a client-rendered shell) and one real, currently-listed individual product/event page. The individual product page directly embeds a full schema.org Event JSON-LD block including price offers.

probe_history.reason: The venue's official domain (so36.com) redirects to /tickets, a server-rendered ticket-shop page built on the 'tickettoaster' platform (assets under /assets/toaster_frontend/, seller name 'tickettoaster GmbH' later confirmed in JSON-LD) — this is the venue's own first-party ticket shop on its own domain, not a third-party aggregator. The page's own hidden SEO fallback nav list ('Die nächsten 10 Termine') is real, server-rendered plain HTML listing each of the next several events as '<title> in Berlin am DD.MM.YYYY' with a link to its own '/produkte/{numeric-id}-tickets-...-am-DD-MM-YYYY' product page (title + date + a numeric per-product id, all directly present). Following one such link to its own individual product page showed it embeds a full, well-formed schema.org Event JSON-LD block (name, startDate WITH a correct +02:00 Berlin summer offset, endDate, location with full address, image, description, and multiple priced Offer entries) directly in server-rendered HTML — sufficient to answer the investigation question without any structural/browser escalation.

venue_reference: SO36 (legendary punk/alternative music club, Oranienstraße 190, Kreuzberg, Berlin, near Heinrichplatz)

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from retained evidence: the product page's own JSON-LD 'location' names 'SO36' at 'Oranienstraße 190, 10999 Berlin' — matching independently-known venue facts (Oranienstraße, Kreuzberg, near Heinrichplatz).

site_classification.platform: A Ruby application fronted by a shop platform called 'tickettoaster' (assets under /assets/toaster_frontend/; seller organization in JSON-LD offers is 'tickettoaster GmbH', https://www.tickettoaster.de) — this is the venue's own first-party white-label ticket shop on its own so36.com domain, not a third-party ticketing aggregator. Individual product/event pages embed schema.org Event JSON-LD directly.

title.notes: The sampled product page's own JSON-LD 'name' field. Note this source's own 'name' field bundles venue+date into the title text itself; the listing page's own separate title text ('BURNING BERLIN') is the cleaner event-only title and matches this.

start_date.notes: The sampled product page's own JSON-LD 'startDate', a full ISO 8601 datetime with a CORRECT Berlin summer UTC offset (+02:00, CEST) — unlike a comparable field observed at Lido Berlin in this same trial, which appears to hardcode a wrong offset.

time.notes: Time-of-day + offset portion of the same 'startDate' field.

end.notes: The sampled product page's own JSON-LD 'endDate' field.

venue_location.notes: The sampled product page's own JSON-LD 'location.name'/'location.address' (streetAddress/addressLocality/postalCode/addressCountry, all present).

source_record_id.notes: The listing page's own fallback nav directly states each event's numeric product id as part of its own permalink ('/produkte/98733-tickets-burning-berlin-so36-berlin-am-26-08-2026') — this is the site's own first-party product identifier, used as its own canonical URL path segment, matching the policy's 'derived from a deterministic source property whose own stability is itself evidenced (a permalink URL slug the source uses as its own canonical path)' rule.

event_url.notes: The listing page's own real anchor href for this event's product page; independently confirmed by successfully fetching that exact URL and finding the matching JSON-LD Event block.

price.notes: The sampled product page's own JSON-LD 'offers' array — 3 distinct priced ticket-variant Offers (all EUR), each with its own 'seller' (tickettoaster GmbH, the venue's own first-party shop platform) and 'availability' (SoldOut for this sampled, already-passed-by-observation-date event).

reasons: Identity PROVEN directly from retained first-party evidence.
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved supported class; a CONFIRMED public data path retained (the shop listing's own fallback nav, leading to a JSON-LD-bearing product page).

title, start_date, end, venue_location, source_record_id, event_url and price ALL PROVEN via DIRECT_SOURCE from a single retained product page — the richest, cleanest single-page sample of the six venues in this trial.
recommended_family JSON_LD (an existing, already-implemented, reusable module — ingestion/json-ld/).
